**Finding submitted: deviation (medium severity).**

**What I found.** The audit right binding us lives in Article II.IV(b) (p0073), with its cost-allocation sentence displaced up at p0064. There is no audit heading, so this matches the planner's suspicion that the right was buried in the volume-billing/record-keeping terms.

**Elements already at or above the playbook position:**
- Independent CPA or audit professional, selected by mutual agreement
- Scope limited to "appropriate accounting records" — no right of access to our systems
- 30-day lead time from Licensor's written request
- Licensor bears cost unless a discrepancy over 5% is found (preferred threshold, not just the 10% fallback)

**Why it still fails the fallback:** no frequency cap whatsoever. Licensor could serve repeated audit requests, which is unlimited-audit / walk-away territory and misses the fallback's "once per year." The clause is also silent on business hours and on binding the third-party auditor to confidentiality — the confidentiality article covers the parties, not an outside CPA.

**Redline (validated ok:true):** a single proviso appended to p0073 capping audits at one per twelve months, requiring 30 days' prior written notice, confining them to normal business hours without unreasonable interference, and binding the auditor to confidentiality no less protective than the Agreement. I deliberately left the 5% cost-shift and the records-only scope untouched, since both already favor us — reopening them risks trading away a better-than-fallback bargain.
